lots.title: Provision of Fire Door Surveys (Fire Door Specification)
lots.description: Lot 4 of London Borough of Bexley Building Services Framework 6278, covering the supply, installation, inspection, testing, certification and maintenance of fire doors and fire door sets in properties under the control of the London Borough of Bexley. Contract commencement: April 2026. The objective is compliance with current UK HSE guidance, the Building Regulations, relevant British Standards, and statutory duties under the Fire Safety Order. Scope includes supply and installation of new FD-rated doors and frames, inspection/testing/certification of existing doors, remedial and maintenance works, provision of test evidence and product data sheets, and updating Authority asset records by uploading documentation to the TF Cloud / Civica compliance platform. Competent installers, fire-rated door set assemblies (including hardware, seals and glazing), annual/quarterly inspection regimes, joint verification at handover and a full commissioning pack are required. Non-conformances are rectified at the contractor's cost.
requirements: Supply and installation of new fire doors and frames to FD30, FD60, FD90 or FD120 ratings per design drawings or fire strategy documents.
For domestic premises, flat entrance doors must be a minimum FD30S rating (30 minutes fire and smoke resistance).
Intumescent and cold smoke seals must be continuous and undamaged; cold smoke brush-type seals required in corridors/staircases providing escape routes to achieve FD30S or FD60S compliance.

All hardware must be fire-rated and tested to the relevant EN standards in force and must form part of the tested and approved door set assembly, including self-closing devices to BS EN 1154, hinges, and compliant signage ('Fire Door - Keep Shut / Locked').
Any glazing must use fire-rated glass installed with approved fire-resistant glazing systems.
Installation must be carried out by competent installers trained in fire door installation.
All fire doors must be inspected as a minimum annually.
Communal fire doors in domestic premises must be checked quarterly in accordance with the Fire Safety (England) Regulations 2022.
Inspections must include checks for leaf/frame integrity, gaps, seals, signage, and correct closer operation.

Contractor must submit installation service sheets, inspection logs, photographs and asset schedules for each fire door, with all documents uploaded to TF Cloud / Civica for full audit trail and compliance verification.
Contractors must be competent and trained in the installation of fire doors and frames including all door furniture.
Risk Assessments and Method Statements must be approved before work begins.
On completion of any repair or installation works the contractor must carry out a joint verification inspection with a London Borough of Bexley representative.
A final installation and commissioning pack including a door-by-door register and all compliance documents must be provided.
Non-conformances must be rectified at the contractor's cost.

Inspection checklist must cover: door leaf condition; frame condition and fixings; gaps within tolerance (<=4mm); intumescent/smoke seals continuous and undamaged; self-closer operates effectively; signage correctly fitted; no obstructions or alterations affecting performance; overall pass/fail compliance rating.

Fire door asset schedule must capture: Property/Block Name, Door Location, Fire Rating (FD30/FD60), Door Type/Material, Installation Date, Inspection Date, Findings, Action Taken, Certification Reference.
Installation & Inspection Certificate must record: Certificate No, Door ID, Location, Installer, Date Installed, Fire Rating, Smoke Seal (Yes/No), Inspector Signature, Date of Inspection.
